content.text:
I submitted **index 28** (Ca 0.267, Mn 0.733), which gave the highest photocurrent I measured: 1.73e-6 A. All 3 merit measurements are used; I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Ca fraction | Nearest known phase (predicted band gap) | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.412 | Ca2Mn3O8 (2.69 eV) | 4e-8 A |
| 3 | 0.333 | CaMn2O4 (2.54 eV) | 1e-7 A |
| 28 | 0.267 | Between CaMn2O4 and CaMn3O6 (1.65 eV) | 1.73e-6 A |

Photocurrent rose steadily as the composition got richer in Mn. That fits the band-gap predictions: Mn-rich phases have smaller gaps, so they should absorb more of the 3.22 eV light. The stability model puts both Ca2Mn3O8 and CaMn2O4 on the convex hull, so both should be stable. I ruled out the Ca-rich end because CaMnO3 is predicted to be nearly metallic (0.19 eV gap), and the measured trend was falling in that direction.

Index 28 is the most Mn-rich composition in the library, and the trend was still climbing there. So the best measured value may simply be where the library ends, not a true peak. Index 16 has the same composition and wasn't measured separately. This conclusion rests on only three points, and with no XRD taken, I haven't confirmed which phase is actually present at index 28.
